answer: Each identity is announced by a single raven: a one-time admission proof that can never be reused, so no agent claims two origins. The network builds a wharf where every arrival ties to a unique behavior record, and duplicate behavior from one origin is flagged at the dock. Attestation history is written onto shale, recorded cumulatively and unerasable without breaking the stack. Since a raven is unique and each shale layer is public, an attacker must mint a new raven per clone, and wharf detection makes the cluster visible at once.
